standard_prerequisites.name: The sheaf condition for presheaves with values in C is stated via the equalizer of a parallel pair, with F(U) mapping to the equalizer E (definition-sheaf-values-in-category)
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the equalizer diagram and the map whose invertibility is equivalent to the sheaf condition.

core_obligations: If F is a sheaf, F(U) is the equalizer of the parallel pair (proof lines 1011-1013); applying F, which commutes with limits, makes F(F(U)) the equalizer of the corresponding diagram of sets, which is precisely the sheaf condition for the underlying presheaf of sets (proof lines 1013-1015). Conversely assume F(F) is a sheaf; let E be the equalizer in C of the parallel pair (proof lines 1017-1019). The presheaf structure gives a canonical map F(U) -> E (proof lines 1019-1021). Applying F, the map F(F(U)) -> F(E) is an isomorphism because F(F) is a sheaf, i.e. F(F(U)) is the set-equalizer (proof lines 1021-1024). Since F reflects isomorphisms, F(U) -> E is an isomorphism, so F is a sheaf (proof lines 1024-1028).
proof_roadmap: Forward: transfer the sheaf condition through F commuting with equalizers (proof lines 1011-1015).
Converse: the canonical map to the C-equalizer is an isomorphism on F, reflected back to C (proof lines 1017-1028).
